# Naval reporting after dissolution of the Seekriegsleitung

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and verification](../../experiments/corpus_joint/README.md)

**Record:** p205 B, two parts, intercepted on 17 November 1918 with the internal date `16/11`. **Result:** the unchanged Nov16–18 partial key fixes **269 of 271 plaintext positions** from all **542 printed coordinates**. The order ends submission of the daily reports and war diaries to the dissolved command, while requiring offices to continue keeping their diaries.

## Most likely reading

> Mit Auflösung der Seekriegsleitung fallen die bisher dahin erstatteten Tagesmeldungen fort. Das gleiche gilt für Vorlage der Kriegstagebücher. Kriegstagebücher [s]ind von allen Dienststellen vorläufig weiterzuführen. Gleichlautend Ost-, Nordflotte, BMK. Admiralstab 1… Op. Eins.

**English meaning:** With dissolution of the Naval Warfare Command, the daily reports previously sent there are discontinued. The same applies to submission of the war diaries. Every office is to continue maintaining its war diary for the time being. The closing names further addressees and gives an Admiral Staff reference whose second digit remains unknown.

Punctuation, word spacing and the separation of the compact addressee string are editorial. The repeated `KRIEGSTAGEBUECHER` is meaningful: one sentence concerns submitting the diaries, and the next concerns continuing to maintain them. It is therefore retained. `BMK` is not expanded to a specific office on the strength of this ciphertext alone.

## Direct reading and one explicit emendation

```text
MITXAUFLOESUNGXDERXSEEKRIEGSLEITUNGXFALLENXDIEXBISHERXDAHINXERSTATTETENXTAGESMELDUNGENXFORTXDASGLEICHEXGILTXFUERXVORLAGEXDERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHER
?INDXVONXALLENXDIENSTSTELLENXVORLAEUFIGXWEITERZUFUEHRENXGLEICHLAUTENDXOSTNORDFLOTTEXBMKXADMIRALSTABX1?XOPXEINSX
```

Part B1's **160/160 positions** are fixed. Part B2 fixes **109/111**. Its initial unknown is the square cell `GD`, whose possible values under the published partial square are `03456789`. Consequently, `SIND` cannot be obtained by completing an unassigned square cell: `S` is already established at `GA`. The proposed initial `S` requires the single source-coordinate change **B2 index 128 `D → A`**. All other 221 B2 coordinates remain unchanged, and the final unknown digit is left unresolved.

This is a readable editorial reconstruction with an exact one-coordinate cost, not a complete unchanged-source decipherment. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json) supplies the two raw texts, all plaintext domains and the edit map.

## Source and credit

The [p205 B image](../../experiments/corpus_joint/sources/p205_B.png) contains 320 coordinates in B1 and 222 in B2. The extra internal space in B1's printed `V AAFX` does not remove a coordinate. The B2 groups `GXXAV`, `FGAXA` and `DDXDV` were checked at higher magnification; their letters are preserved in the source transcription even where the result suggests a copying error.

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p. 205, PDF p. 208 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The header reads `ASO v LP (6.38 a.m., November 17th)`, `FUER ASO 1655 (16/11) 2 TEILE B M K SEBASTOPOL`.

The **Nov16–18** period key retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json) to **George Lasry** and the historical/research work of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source assembly, review, exact edit costs and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/build_readings.py \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_inputs.json \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/verify_p205.py
```

# p164 B — Dismantling the station and marching to Temesvar

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md)

**Status:** 69/70 raw positions fixed; two explicit coordinate substitutions
in the readable edition; one time digit remains conditional. **Source edition
and review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Period key:** George Lasry and
colleagues.

## Most likely reading

> Wir abbauen 9.11., 0{5/6}00, Weitermarsch Temesvar. Wenn dort aufgebaut,
> rufen wir.

**Meaning:** The station will be dismantled, followed by an onward march to
Temesvar; it will call again once set up there. The literal cipher-only time is
05:00 or 06:00. Under the already documented historical completion of the
November 7–9 square, it is **05:00 on 9 November**.

The telegram style is retained; *wir bauen ab* is the ordinary German wording.
The proposed month `11` repairs the raw `18`. The proposed `RUFEN` repairs raw
`RUDEN`. Both changes are individually costed below.

## Source

Childs, printed p. 164 / PDF p. 167, section B:

```text
LP v ZON (3.34 a.m., November 9th)
1133
RIZI-140

AVGVA XXXXX DFAGG VAAXG VVDXD VVVVG VVVGV AXAFA
XAGGD VVAAX FDDXD XGVAD XXAVD DADVD DVGVX XVXGX
DDDDX DFVVD XDAVV GVGGF VXVVV VFGGD DDDAD XXVGX
VDFGX VDVDX GVVAV AGAGA
```

All 140 coordinates are legible; the received length agrees with the header.
The source marker is printed `RIZI`, not silently normalized to `RICHI`.

## Unchanged-key raw reading

```text
WIRXABBAUEN9X18X0?00WEITERMARSCHXTEMESVARXWENNDORTAUFGEBAUTXRUDENXWIRX
```

The unknown plaintext position 17 is the square cell `XA`, whose baseline
domain is exactly `56`. It is not a lost source coordinate. Every other
position is fixed by the published key and literal transcript.

| Proposed correction | Plaintext position | Received-coordinate change |
|---|---:|---|
| Month `18` → `11` | 14 | Source position 92: `A` → `G` |
| `RUDEN` → `RUFEN` | 62 | Source position 76: `V` → `X` |

All indices are zero-based. The source header supports the November reading;
the verb is a language-based repair. There are **two known-coordinate
substitutions, no erasure fills**, and 138 coordinates remain unchanged.

## Conditional time digit

The existing
[historical square layer](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
gives `VF=6`, `XA=5`, from the independently identified 6th Reserve Division.
Using that same global square assigns `XA=5` here and gives `0500` without any
additional ciphertext change. The baseline square and its `{5,6}` alternative
remain intact. Accepting the date and verb repairs does not require accepting
this separate historical inference.

The proposed edition under that layer is:

```text
WIRXABBAUEN9X11X0500WEITERMARSCHXTEMESVARXWENNDORTAUFGEBAUTXRUFENXWIRX
```

It re-encrypts exactly to the two-substitution ciphertext.

## Evidence and credit

The [source crop](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/sources/childs_p164_B.png),
[literal inputs](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/inputs.json) and
[exact certificate](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/certificates.json)
retain the full evidence. The period key is prior Lasry-team work; the present
source edition and arithmetic review are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-historical-decipherment priority is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/withdrawal_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

# October Caucasus traffic — Kress, Westernhagen and a shipment for Poti

[All readings](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source and verification](../../experiments/october_caucasus/README.md)

**Source edition and repair analysis:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Earlier key:** the published October 4–6 square and 22-column transposition, credited to Childs and George Lasry / Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker in the [key catalogue](../../data/keys.json).

Twelve source records cover seven exchanges about the Caucasus: personnel and money for Kress's delegation, price instructions to Westernhagen, electrical equipment sent to Tiflis, a cargo leaving Braila for Poti, radio timings, a liaison officer and equipment procurement. The p68 procurement pair has a **provisional, heavily repaired first part and an opening-only second part**; it is not a direct recovery of the complete exchange. Another interrupted continuation is retained separately without an accepted reading. The German readings below use explicit editorial repairs. Every received coordinate, surviving garble, ambiguous layout and repair cost is retained in the [certificate](../../experiments/october_caucasus/certificates.json). This is a new reproducible edition in this repository, without a first-historical-decipherment claim.

## p72 A — Reinforcements, administrative personnel and money for Kress

**Source:** printed p. 72 / PDF p. 75, section A, three parts. `COS v OSM (--------, October 9th); NR 294 KRESS (6) 2040 3 TLE`. The heading is **6 October 1918**. The clear route is OSM to COS, with Kress named in the header; it does not make Kress the sender.

### Most likely readable German

> Zu Tel. 30.9. [NATEKS] Nr. 8557. 1. Verstärkung der Deleg. von O.H.L. ohne Beteiligung [… K.M.] angeordnet. 2. Mit Bericht vom 8.[?], [4A] Nr. 553 angeford. Verw.-Pers. wird mit Ausnahme der Garnison-Verw.-Beamten — vergl. Tel. 26.[?], [unresolved reference] — zur Verfügung gestellt werden. 3. Notwendiges Geld ist sichergestellt.

**Meaning:** Reinforcement of the delegation has been ordered by Supreme Army Command, without the participation of an office whose abbreviation is damaged. Requested administrative personnel will be made available, except for garrison-administration officials. Necessary money has been secured.

`Deleg.`, `O.H.L.`, `Verw.-Pers.` and `Garnison-Verw.-Beamten` are expanded only in the explanation. The reference text `NATEKS`, the raw `?SKXM` office abbreviation, and several dates and numbers remain unresolved. The edition does not identify a particular ministry or assign the damaged reference digits.

### What the three source parts preserve

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| A1 | 203 / 178 | 88/89 | The second copy of an identical 25-coordinate run is visibly struck out. | 1 known-coordinate substitution; no asserted fill |
| A2 | 251 / 226 | 108/113 common to both models; 109/113 in one model | An unmarked 25-slot near-repeat; two deletion alternatives remain. | 6 substitutions; 1 or 2 asserted fills |
| A3 | 124 / 124 | 60/62 | Two invalid/missing source coordinates; unchanged geometry | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

The A1 strikeout is a source instruction. The A2 deletion is a reconstruction hypothesis: its adjacent copies differ only by a printed `X` versus a non-coordinate `S`. Removing either copy gives the same raw text except for `GARNISON` versus `G?RNISON`. Both are kept; the latter does not become an independently witnessed `A`.

The raw core is already recognizable as `VERSTAER1UNGDERDELEGXVONOXHXLXOHNEBETEILIGUNG...ANGEORDNET`, and A3 directly contains `ZURVERFUEGUN...GESTELLT...` and most of `NOTWENDIGESGELDISTSICHERGESTELLT`. The stated costs account for making those words readable; the uncorrected strings remain in the certificate.

## p70 A — Westernhagen, price limits and an urgent return

**Source:** printed p. 70 / PDF p. 73, section A, two parts. `POT, COS v NKJ (3.10 a.m., October 7th); FUR COS DEUTSCHE DELEGATO WIRTCHI ABTLG 2305 (6) 2 TLE`.

### Most likely readable German

> An Westernhagen. Bestätigen Telegr. 28.9. Euer früheres Telegr. nicht erhalten. Da von euch ohne Bericht und Kenntnis dortiger Marktlage gelassen, können Preisgrenzen nicht aufgeben. Mdl. Rücksprache sofort erforderlich. Bitten Rückkehr beschleunigen. Drahten Gleiches über ASTO Constanza. Bestätigt Empfang. Deutkauf.

**Meaning:** A telegram of 28 September is acknowledged, but an earlier one was not received. Without the requested report or knowledge of local market conditions, the sender cannot give price limits. An immediate personal discussion is needed; Westernhagen is asked to hasten his return. The same instruction is being telegraphed via `ASTO Constanza`, and receipt is to be acknowledged.

The source names only **Westernhagen**. `MDL` is interpreted as *mündliche*; `ASTO` and the signature `DEUTKAUF` are retained without an institutional expansion. The encrypted spelling is `RUECKEHR` with one `K`; ordinary German spelling in the displayed reading supplies the second `k` as a prose normalization. The unusual but directly decoded `AUFGEBEN` remains; the edition does not silently substitute a more idiomatic verb.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| A1 | 332 / 322 | 156/161 | Two separate identical five-coordinate pairs: `AAAAA AAAAA` and `DAAGG DAAGG` | 7 substitutions; 5 fills |
| A2 | 246 / 246 | 121/123 | Header says `RICHI-256`; the printed 246-slot body decodes at its actual length | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

Removing one copy of each repeated A1 group gives four source-index aliases and **one identical 322-coordinate stream**. Those deletions are conditional, despite the visible repetition. A2 is not padded by ten invented coordinates to force its length to match the header: its raw reading already begins `MDLXRUECKSPRACHEDOFORTERFORDERLICH...` and ends `...EMPFANGXDEUTKAUF` at 246 slots.

## p71 A1 — Electrical equipment sent to Tiflis

**Source:** printed p. 71 / PDF p. 74, section A, first of two parts. `POT v OSM (01.17 a.m., October 8th); FUR COS (6) 1230 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-170`. The page heading is **6 October 1918**.

### Most likely readable German

> Nach Tiflis abgegangen 28.9., mit 2 Begleiter: 2 Stück 16-kW-Maschinensätze und 1 20-kW-Umformer.

**Meaning:** Two machine sets rated at 16 kW and one converter, provisionally read as rated at 20 kW, were dispatched to Tiflis on 28 September with two accompanying people. The directly decoded telegraphic form is `BEGLEITER`; no grammatical final `N` is inserted into the cipher edition.

The literal **170 slots** have unchanged geometry and fix **72/85 raw positions**. Twelve printed dashes and one damaged `C`-shaped glyph in row one's last group are treated as erasures. That glyph may be an incomplete `G`, but the raw letter domain remains open. The proposed reading fills all **13 erasures** and changes **one known coordinate**, source slot 40 from `G` to `X`, to repair the raw `GEGA?BEN` fragment to `GEGANGEN`. All slot and plaintext positions in the certificate are zero-based.

The two equipment counts, the **16-kW** rating, and the date digits `28` and `9` survive directly. The **2** in the proposed **20-kW** rating is an erasure fill, so the exact second rating is conditional. The raw ending is `...UND1??0KX?XUMFORMER`, not a fully recovered numerical specification.

Part A2 advertises **192 coordinates** but stops after **85**, followed by the printed note `(interference)`. Under the simple hypothesis that the lost suffix supplies the remaining 107 slots, no complete plaintext letter is fixed: each surviving symbol supplies only one side of a coordinate pair. Its literal fragment and conditional letter domains are preserved separately. It contributes neither a new accepted reading nor inferred equipment details.

## p69 B — Violetta's cargo from Braila to Poti

**Source:** printed p. 69 / PDF p. 72, section B, two parts. `COS v NKJ (---- October 11th); NR 298 FUR COS HPTM GEMOLL (6) 2330 2 TLE`. The page heading says **5 October**, while the individual clear header says `(6)`; both are preserved.

### Most likely readable German

> Ab Braila 4.10. mit D. Violetta: 10 000 Eierhandgranaten, 3 Wagen Masch.-Gew., [04WLI] russ. Gew., 9 Wag. Mun., [94TS6] Lebensmittel, 16 Faß Benzin, 2 Kisten Kuriergepäck, 10 Wag. Mun. für Mun.-Dep. Poti und mehrere Wag. für dort. Truppen.

**Meaning:** A cargo sent from Braila aboard the vessel *Violetta* includes hand grenades, machine guns, Russian rifles, ammunition, food, petrol and courier luggage. Poti's ammunition depot and troops there are named as destinations. Two damaged quantity fields are unresolved. The proposed **10 000** hand grenades is also conditional: the common raw reading is `100?0`, and the fourth digit depends on the declared alignment and an erased-coordinate fill. It is not an independently established exact quantity.

The displayed **4.10.** date and several words are editorial repairs. `04WLI` and `94TS6` are raw garbles, not accepted quantities; no numerical expansion is supplied for them. `D.`, `Masch.-Gew.`, `russ. Gew.`, `Wag.` and `Mun.-Dep.` are interpreted in their cargo context. The text does not independently establish the ship's registry or the nature of the wagons carried.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Raw positions fixed across every tested placement | Source issue | Minimum additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| B1 | 329 / 330 | 159/165 | Four-letter group `VXFX`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 9 substitutions; 2 fills |
| B2 | 65 / 66 | 28/33 | Four-letter group `(X)FFF`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 1 substitution; 1 fill |

These models supply a slot because a printed group is short and the header is one longer. They do not prove that the historical loss occurred there. In B1 the editorial template has two tied minimum-cost placements. In B2, the proposed complete continuation is

```text
UNDMEHREREWAGXFUERDORTXTRUPPENXXX
```

It replaces the short printed `XFFF` by `GDFFF`: either insert `G` before the printed `X` and change that `X` to `D`, or change `X` to `G` and insert `D` after it. Both have exactly one known-coordinate substitution and one missing-coordinate fill. All five within-group placements, including the more expensive ones, remain in the certificate.

## p72 B — Radio timings and reception

**Source:** printed p. 72 / PDF p. 75, section B. `POT v OSM (---------, October 9th); FUR POT (6) 0830; RIZI-274`. The source prints `RIZI`; that label is not silently rewritten as `RICHI`.

### Most likely readable German

> Zu dort Nr. 479: 20.00, 20.30 für OSM ungeeignet. Sind Sie mit RICHI [M98], 30.9., mitgeteilten Zeiten einverstanden? Wie ist dort Empfang OSM, Welle 2800 und 3500? Schlee.

**Meaning:** The proposed times are unsuitable for OSM. The recipient is asked whether the previously notified times are acceptable and how OSM is received at two wavelengths.

The unchanged 274-coordinate geometry fixes **136/137 raw positions**. The displayed `NR`, `2000`, `SIE` and `3500` require **four known-coordinate substitutions**, with one additional erased-coordinate fill for `ZU`. The first time and second wavelength are plausible editorial values, not independently recovered numerical facts. `2030`, `2800` and `SCHLEE` are directly decoded; the damaged reference `RICHIM98` is left unresolved.

## p69 A — A liaison officer from Army Group Kiev

**Source:** printed p. 69 / PDF p. 72, section A. `NKJ v --- (---- October 11th); NR 44 0628 (5.10); RICHI-220`. The sender is not identified in the clear header.

### Most likely readable German

> Mit Einverständnis O.H.L. wird Rittm. [Tellner?], [Tellner?], als Verbdgs.-Offz. der Heeresgr. nach Tiflis entsandt. Heergr. Kjew.

**Meaning:** With Supreme Army Command's approval, a cavalry captain is being sent to Tiflis as the army group's liaison officer. The signature names Army Group Kiev; the cipher's literal spelling is `KJEW`. The damaged surname is repeated and is provisionally read as **Tellner**, without assigning a forename or identifying a person outside the telegram.

The actual body has **220 coordinates**, matching the header. Three parenthesized `X` values are retained as recorded source coordinates, including the final printed run `FDX(X)-X(X)VGX`. Parentheses remain visible in the literal row edition. Removing those annotated letters or treating the ten-slot run as one five-letter group would change the frame.

The literal inverse fixes **109/110 raw positions**:

```text
MITEINVERSTAEWDNISXOXHXLXWIRDRITTMXTELLNEIXTELLN1RXA?SVERBDGSXXBFZDERHEERELGRXNACHXTIKLCSXEN5SAND6XHEERGRXKJEW
```

The displayed ordinary words require **10 known-coordinate substitutions and one erased-coordinate fill**. The two raw surname copies, `TELLNEI` and `TELLN1R`, preserve complementary letters: `TELLNER` combines the sixth letter of the first copy with the seventh of the second. That is still an editorial reconstruction, not an independent personnel identification. `RITTM`, `VERBDGS` and `OFFZ` are expanded only in the explanation.

## p68 A — Provisional procurement text carrying CHI labels

**Source:** printed p. 68 / PDF p. 71, section A, two parts. `COS, POT v NKJ (9.19 p.m., October 5th); VON THO 1640 (5) 2 TEILE`. The first part visibly says **CHI-220**. The second says **CHI-186** and then **RICHI-186** on the next line. Those labels are preserved exactly.

The published October 4–6 key gives a recognizable Kress/Tiflis address and equipment vocabulary. This is another warning that the printed `CHI` label alone does not identify the separate key family used by the open/previously open CHI challenges. These parts are not companions under the recovered p153 key.

### Provisional first-part reading

> General v. Kress, Tiflis. Zu T-Spruch Nr. [?159; damaged reference]. Betr. Entsendung 2 Offz. nach Tiflis zum Ankauf von Ausrüstungsstücken …

**Meaning under the proposed repairs:** The message concerns sending two officers to Tiflis to purchase equipment. Its reference number and date cannot be completed responsibly from this edition.

The literal **220-slot** body has **22 coordinate erasures**, including the non-coordinate letters `W` and `K`, and fixes **89/110 raw positions**. Two erased coordinates fall in the same plaintext pair. Its unchanged inverse is:

```text
G?NE??LOKR?SSXTIFL?LXX?1TSP?UC6NR?159F????9XBZTRW?NT?1?DU?G2OFFX0NAUHDTCFSISXZU??XKAUFVONA5SR5?STUNAS?TS?CKENX
```

The displayed ordinary wording needs **24 known-coordinate substitutions and 17 erased-coordinate fills**. This substantial editorial cost is why the reading remains **provisional**. The `T` in `TSPRUCH` survives directly and is not expanded to an asserted original abbreviation. Five date/reference positions and the first position after `NR` remain unassigned in the proposed template. No precise reference date is supplied.

### Limited second-part continuation

Part 2 has exactly **186 slots**, with **41 coordinate erasures** and **56/93 fixed raw positions**. Its beginning `??DARTILLER??T7QITJO?` supports the provisional continuation:

> … und Artilleriemunition …

The template asserts only `UNDARTILLERIEMUNITION`, requiring **four known-coordinate substitutions and five erasure fills**. The remaining **72 plaintext positions are unasserted**. The certificate retains their raw domains, and its arbitrary coordinate fillers for a complete arithmetic roundtrip are not promoted to a further sentence, quantity, date or signature.

## Relation to the open p73 challenge

These messages add readable traffic from the Kress/Caucasus route, with explicit October origin and later interception dates. They supply neither p73's key nor a matching plaintext passage. **p73 remains open**; the source-level repairs here do not decide between its conflicting 26 October and 8 November date layers.

# October staffing, manganese purchases and service traffic

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md)

**Status:** Six source-reviewed records under the previously published
**Oct4–6 key**. The principal result is a two-part Bavarian personnel order;
four other records concern Tiflis unit information, medical retransmission,
manganese purchases and a telegram acknowledgment. Source review:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier key credit belongs to **J. Rives
Childs**, **George Lasry**, and **Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker**.

All six printed frames have their advertised lengths. Across 1,264 received
slots, the raw key inverse fixes 630 of 632 plaintext positions. The edition
uses **four explicit known-coordinate substitutions and two erasure fills**;
626 proposed characters need neither. The
[reproducible source package](../../experiments/october_staffing/README.md)
contains every source row, domain, coordinate origin, edit and re-encryption.
There is no new key claim or proposed p73 plaintext.

## p66 C1 and p67 A2 — Bavarian command appointments

The source explicitly joins these parts: both carry `NR40 DEUTSCHE DELEGATION
KAUKASUS1723(5)2TLE`, with `1TL RICHI-286` on p66 and `2TL RICHI-220` on p67.
Both travel `COS v NKJ`; the reception times are 03.15 and 03.21 a.m. on
October 6. The page heading is October 5, and the shared origin field is
`1723(5)`.

**Most likely German reading, with abbreviation and reference fields retained:**

> Oberst und Kdeur des 4. bayr. Chev.-Regt., Graf von Seyboltstorff, als
> Kdeur der 4. bayr. Kav.-Brig. bestimmt, ist sofort zu dieser Brig. zu
> beordern. Abreisetag umgehend drahten.
>
> Als Ersatz ist bereits Oberstlt. Karl von Grundherr, röm.I, des 4.
> Chev.-Regts dorthin beordert. Bayr. Kriegsministerium Nr 249774P.

The order directs the named colonel to the 4th Bavarian Cavalry Brigade and
requests the departure date. The second part says that the named lieutenant
colonel has already been ordered there as the replacement. Both brigade and
regiment numerals **4**, `KARLVONGRUNDHERR`, and the name discriminator `ROEM1`
are directly fixed by the received coordinates. The text alone does not locate
the brigade or identify a later telegram's unknown brigade numeral.

The raw first part spells the surname `SEYBOLTSTORF0`; its final `0` becomes
`F` through one coordinate substitution. The second part has `BEORSERT`;
`BEORDERT` costs one coordinate substitution. The reference `249774P` is
preserved without adding punctuation or interpreting its final character.

The institutional
[SLUB catalogue](https://katalog.slub-dresden.de/en/id/0-165780514X) records a 1922
history of the 4th Chevaulegers with contributors **Karl von Grundherr** and
**August Graf von Freyen-Seyboltstorff**. This supplies bibliographic support
for the names. Its linked WLB scan was unavailable to automated access during
this review; no command date or troop movement from that book is asserted.
The telegram's shorter surname form remains the form used in the reading.

Sources: [p66 C1](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p66_C1.png)
and [p67 A2](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p67_A2.png).

## p66 B — Repeat the garbled medical telegram

Header: `--- v NKJ (3.11 a.m., October 6th); DEUTSCHE DELEGATION KAUKASUS
1812(5); RICHI-284`.

## Historical identification: most likely the 6th Reserve Division

The French telegram and German calendar were already audited in the repository's [p176b unit-history review](../../data/reviews/p176b_unit_context.json). The new application here is to the newly source-edited p166/p167/p170 B reports and the **different November 7–9 square**. The earlier p176b plaintext and its 217/219/6 contextual reading retain their published attribution.

**A contemporary operational telegram supports the reading 6.** General Franchet d'Esperey's telegram **5.956/3**, sent from Salonique to Clemenceau and Foch on **19 November 1918 at 22:40**, describes the situation on **11 November**. Its paragraph on the reconstituted German 11th Army names the Alpenkorps, the 217th and 219th divisions around Nagy-Backskerek–Verschatz, and explicitly the **6th Reserve Division**. The relevant short passage reads: “217° — 219° D.I. Nagy-Backskerek—Verschatz) 6° D.I. réserve”. The matching formations and geography support the same identification in these German reports of 9 November; the French telegram is two days later in its reported situation and ten days later in transmission.

This is **document 39, printed p. 79** (document pp. 79–82; PDF p. 153) in *Documents diplomatiques français sur l'histoire du Bassin des Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I, *Octobre 1918 – Août 1919*, documents collected by Magda Ádám, György Litván and Mária Ormos, edited by Magda Ádám, Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest, **1993**, ISBN 963 05 6659 1.
